biography.plain_text: Valentin Zavadnikov is a Russian businessman and former senator whose investments included a substantial stake in the spirits producer Synergy. Originally trained in maritime engineering, he worked in commercial shipping before moving into finance and energy management. He also became a founding partner of the Moscow School of Management Skolkovo.

confidence.reason: Direct first-person account and contemporary business reporting support the selected durable facts.

long_biography.plain_text:
Valentin Zavadnikov wanted the Moscow School of Management Skolkovo to connect students with working businesses. As a founding partner, he helped develop plans for an entrepreneurial community around the school, giving students opportunities to join start-ups and larger projects. He also advised its president, Andrei Rappoport.

His own early ventures included a wood-processing plant on Sakhalin. After a forest fire, he and his partners combined international funding for forest renewal with equipment made available during the expansion of Japan's Niigata airport. The plant processed salvageable timber and exported it to Japan.
